exploring-midjourney-v7-style-codes.intro: This Midjourney prompt pairs a custom descriptive phrase — like "May the prompt be with you" — with the --sref (style reference) parameter pointing to reference image ID 210208245. The resulting image adopts the visual DNA of that reference: color palette, linework density, rendering texture, and overall illustrative mood — while the subject matter comes from whatever descriptive text you place before the --sref tag. The output is a 1:1 square composition, which frames the illustration tightly with no distracting borders, making it ideal for avatar art, social media posts, or concept thumbnails. This prompt is aimed at beginners who want consistent stylistic output without manually reverse-engineering every visual parameter. howTo.title: Adjust style reference strength if needed
howTo.body: If the output strays too far from the reference style, increase influence by adding --sw 100 (default is 100). Lower values let your descriptive text dominate; higher values push the reference style harder.

howTo.title: Fix muddy or over-styled results

faq.q: Which tool produces the best results with --sref style references?

faq.q: Why does my image look nothing like the reference style?
faq.a: This usually happens when --sw is too low or your descriptive text conflicts with the reference style. Raise --sw toward 100, shorten your subject description to avoid style dilution, and verify that reference image 210208245 is still accessible in Midjourney's system.

Lighting tends toward neutral studio-grade illumination to keep focus on the technical comparison rather than artistic mood. Textures range from grainy or pixelated in the 1K panel to sharp and detail-rich in the 2K panel. The composition often includes labeled callouts or arrows connecting the two stages. This prompt suits technical writers, AI tool reviewers, and developers building documentation pages. It works well for blog headers explaining model architecture, YouTube video thumbnails about diffusion models, or social media posts sharing AI workflow insights. Use the 1:1 aspect ratio for platform versatility across feeds and embeds.

faq.q: Which tool handles subject replacement better, nano-banana-pro or Gemini?

faq.q: Why does my replaced subject look blurry or distorted?

Make sure both reference images are at similar resolutions and keep the strength around 60-75 percent. If the character has fine details like text or facial features, lower the strength and let the model do fewer reconstruction passes.

The 1:1 aspect ratio anchors the output as a square frame, ideal for social media displays or portfolio thumbnails. This prompt is useful for concept artists, 3D illustrators, and visual developers who need rapid style experimentation without manually adjusting lighting or rendering pipelines each time. It works well when building a cohesive lookbook across urban sketching scenes, portrait studies, still-life arrangements, or architectural visualization mockups. The --sref parameter accepts any valid Midjourney style reference ID, meaning the placeholder style value can be swapped freely. Use this when you want consistent lighting language across varied subjects, when a client requests a unified visual direction, or when stress-testing how one style treats completely different subjects. faq.q: Which tool handles this style reference prompt best and why?

faq.q: Why does my output look wrong and how do I fix it?
faq.a: Most failures come from an expired or invalid --sref ID. Verify the style reference ID exists in your Midjourney account or gallery. howTo.body: The most common failure is mis‑rendered sword grip or extra fingers. Inspect the right hand closely; if the sword appears floating or fingers merge, re‑run with an explicit negative prompt like ‘deformed hands, missing fingers, sword not held’ and tighten the pose weight.

variations.prompt: Scene: type: “studio backdrop” camera_angle: “straight on, centered composition” lens: type: “standard 50mm” effects: “soft diffused lighting, neutral gray background” Character: identity: ethnicity: “Japanese” gender: “girl” hair: “Brown medium length hair with cat ears” outfit: style: “windy, dressy, Idol costumes that resemble high school girl uniforms” pose: description: “static, poised stance, both hands lowered” body_orientation: “facing forward directly at camera” Hands_and_Gesture: right_hand: gesture: “resting at side, fingers relaxed” position: “down by her hip” left_hand: gesture: “open hand, palm facing inward” fingers: “all five clearly visible” Lighting: type: “even, shadowless” mood: “calm, serene” Style: “character sheet, clean lines”

variations.label: Cinematic warm‑cool contrast
variations.prompt: Scene: type: “battle scene at dusk” camera_angle: “low angle, looking up” lens: type: “anamorphic widescreen” effects: “volumetric god rays, color contrast between warm sunset and cool shadows” Character: identity: ethnicity: “Japanese” gender: “girl” hair: “Brown medium length hair with cat ears, flowing dynamically” outfit: style: “windy, dressy, Idol costumes that resemble high school girl uniforms, tattered edges” pose: description: “leaping forward, sword raised high” body_orientation: “dynamic diagonal across frame” Hands_and_Gesture: right_hand: gesture: “gripping sword hilt with both hands” position: “above head, blade pointed skyward” left_hand: gesture: “reaching back for balance” fingers: “splayed” Lighting: type: “backlit rim light, dual‑tone” mood: “epic, tense” Style: “anime key visual”

variations.label: Tighter packshot style
variations.prompt: Scene: type: “product showcase” camera_angle: “eye‑level, close‑up portrait” lens: type: “macro 100mm” effects: “shallow depth of field, bokeh background” Character: identity: ethnicity: “Japanese” gender: “girl” hair: “Brown medium length hair with cat ears, sharply focused” outfit: style: “windy, dressy, Idol costumes that resemble high school girl uniforms, fabric details crisp” pose: description: “static, slight turn, one hand on hip” body_orientation: “three‑quarter view” Hands_and_Gesture: right_hand: gesture: “holding a Japanese sword, blade horizontal across body” position: “at waist level” left_hand: gesture: “open hand, palm up” fingers: “neatly arranged” Lighting: type: “studio three‑point” mood: “commercial, polished” Style: “character design sheet, clean white background”
